title: Better Work, Not Better Workers: AI and the Junior Expertise Gap
summary: A three-month RCT with 133 patent lawyers finds AI lifts everyone's drafts, juniors most, but when the tool is taken away only seniors come out with better judgment, and junior skill splits into winners and strugglers. We go through the design, the fragile robustness checks and the mechanism (engagement and time on task), and turn it into tutor modes for Claude skills, with-and-without-tool self-checks, and a Dutch AI-literacy audit idea.
shownotes:
Why measuring AI's effect on expertise is hard: AI is easy to operate but hard to evaluate
The design: 133 patent lawyers at 11 US IP firms, AI-assisted drafting versus unassisted redlining
Result 1: AI raises drafting quality, juniors gain most, fewer poor drafts
Result 2: on unassisted redlining only seniors improve; junior scores bifurcate (springboard versus cushion)
Mechanism: time on task and engagement, with Strömberg et al., Bastani et al. (GPT Tutor) and Shen & Tamkin
How much to trust it: small sample, no baseline test, Google funding, AI-use audit, firm-drop and threshold checks, LLM-as-rater with low per-item correlation
Takeaways: with-tool versus without-tool self-checks, tutor mode and rationale hooks for Claude skills, per-item checks for LLM raters
Dutch business idea: AI-literacy and skill-retention audit for professional-services firms under AI Act Article 4
